assets.useWhen: rendering Markdown or rich text with linkable headings, or building a table of contents. Ids follow GitHub's style: a slug of the heading, and `-1`, `-2`, … for repeats. A heading with no letters or digits gets `section`. The ids come back in the same order as the headings, one per heading.
signatures: export function headingIds(headings: readonly string[]): readonly string[]

assets.name: htmlToPlainText
assets.summary: Turns an HTML fragment into one line of readable text: tags dropped, entities decoded.
assets.useWhen:
rich text from a CMS, an editor or an email has to become a preview, a search index entry or a notification. Paragraphs, list items and `
` become spaces, so `

a

b

` reads `a b`, not `ab`. Scripts and styles go with their contents. Only `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` are decoded; others such as ` ` stay as written. The result is text, not HTML: escape it again before putting it back into markup.
signatures: export function htmlToPlainText(html: string): string

assets.name: listToSentence
assets.summary: Joins items into an English phrase with commas and a final `and` or `or`: `a, b and c`.
assets.useWhen: a message lists several things in prose, such as the fields that failed, the people invited or the formats accepted. Items are trimmed and blank ones skipped. One item comes back alone, two are joined by the word, and no items give `''`. There is no comma before the final word.
signatures: export function listToSentence(items: readonly string[], conjunction: 'and' | 'or'): string
export function listToSentence(conjunction: 'and' | 'or'): (items: readonly string[]) => string

assets.name: listWithOthers
assets.summary: Names the first few items and counts the rest: `Ana, Ben and 3 others`.
assets.useWhen: a compact line such as "liked by", "shared with" or "assigned to" can't list everyone. When only one item would be hidden, it is named instead, since `and 1 other` takes as much room as the name. Names are trimmed and blank ones skipped. No names give `''`.
signatures: export function listWithOthers(names: readonly string[], shown: number): string
export function listWithOthers(shown: number): (names: readonly string[]) => string

assets.name: maskCardNumber
assets.summary: Shows a payment card number as `•••• 4242`, the last four digits behind a fixed mask.
assets.useWhen: listing saved cards, receipts or order details. The mask has the same length for every card, so it hides how many digits there are. Spaces and dashes in the input don't matter. Input with fewer than 12 digits isn't a card number and comes back fully masked as `••••`, so a partial number is never shown.
signatures: export function maskCardNumber(cardNumber: string): string

assets.name: maskEmail
assets.summary: Hides an email address except its first letter and its domain: `j•••@example.com`.
assets.useWhen: showing which address a code or reset link went to, in logs, support tools or confirmation screens, without exposing the whole address. The mask has a fixed length, so it doesn't reveal how long the name is. Anything that isn't an email comes back as `•••`, so a mistyped phone number or token never leaks through.
signatures: export function maskEmail(email: string): string

assets.name: maskMiddle
assets.summary: Hides the middle of a secret, showing a few characters at each end: `sk_l••••9xQz`.
assets.useWhen: displaying an API key, token or account ID so a person can tell which one it is without seeing it. Each end shows at most `visible` characters, and never more than a quarter of the value, so a short secret stays mostly hidden. The mask has a fixed length, so it doesn't reveal how long the secret is.
signatures: export function maskMiddle(secret: string, visible: number): string
export function maskMiddle(visible: number): (secret: string) => string

assets.name: maskPhone
assets.summary: Hides every digit of a phone number but the last four, keeping its punctuation in place.
assets.useWhen: confirming where an SMS code went, or listing contacts in a support tool, where the last digits are enough to recognize the number. Spaces, brackets, dashes and the `+` stay, so the masked number keeps its familiar shape. A value with four digits or fewer is masked completely, since showing four would show all of it.
signatures: export function maskPhone(phone: string): string

assets.name: normalizeSearchQuery
assets.summary: Reduces a search query to lowercase words without accents or punctuation: `cafe creme`.
assets.useWhen: comparing what someone typed with stored text, as a cache key for search results, or before logging queries, so `Café  CRÈME!` and `cafe creme` count as the same search. Run the stored text through it too. Apostrophes are dropped inside words (`don't` → `dont`) and other symbols become spaces, so `c++` and `c#` both become `c`: keep the raw query when symbols matter.
signatures: export function normalizeSearchQuery(query: string): string

assets.name: propertyName
assets.summary: Turns a spreadsheet header or label into a camelCase property name: `First Name` → `firstName`.
assets.useWhen: mapping CSV or form headers to the keys of a JavaScript object or a JSON payload. Accents are dropped, symbols separate words, and existing camelCase keeps its word breaks, so `userID` gives `userId`. A name starting with a digit gets `_` in front so it stays a valid identifier. A header with no letters or digits gives `''`.
signatures: export function propertyName(header: string): string

assets.name: readingTimeMinutes
assets.summary: Estimates how many whole minutes a text takes to read, rounding up: `5` for `5 min read`.
assets.useWhen: a blog post, article or help page shows its reading time. Words are counted by whitespace, so accented and non-Latin words count like any other. Any text with a word in it takes at least one minute; an empty text takes zero. Around 200 to 250 words per minute suits most adults. For HTML, run it through `htmlToPlainText` first.
signatures: export function readingTimeMinutes(text: string, wordsPerMinute: number): number
export function readingTimeMinutes(wordsPerMinute: number): (text: string) => number

assets.name: renderTemplate
assets.summary: Fills `{{name}}` placeholders from values, or reports every placeholder left without one.
assets.useWhen: a message must not go out half-filled, such as a transactional email, an SMS or a legal notice, and the error should list everything missing at once rather than one key per attempt. A value that is absent, `null` or `undefined` counts as missing. Placeholders are `{{word}}`, with no spaces inside the braces.
signatures: export function renderTemplate( text: string, values: RenderTemplateValues, ): Result<string, RenderTemplateError>
export function renderTemplate( values: RenderTemplateValues, ): (text: string) => Result<string, RenderTemplateError>

assets.name: safeFileName
assets.summary: Makes a string safe to use as a file name on Windows, macOS and Linux, keeping it readable.
assets.useWhen: saving an upload, an export or a generated report under a name a user typed or a title from your data. Slashes, backslashes, colons and pipes become `-`; other forbidden characters go. Whitespace collapses, leading and trailing dots and spaces go, reserved Windows names such as `CON` get a `_` in front, and the part before the extension is cut to 100 characters. The extension is kept. A name with nothing left becomes `untitled`.
signatures: export function safeFileName(name: string): string

assets.name: searchHighlight
assets.summary: Wraps every word of a search query found in a text in `<mark>`, returning safe HTML.
assets.useWhen: showing search results with the matched words highlighted, where both the text and the query come from users. Each query word is matched on its own, in any case and order, longest first, so `java script` marks both words and `javascript` isn't cut short by `java`. The text is HTML-escaped piece by piece, so a query such as `amp` can't land inside `&` and a `<script>` in the text stays inert.
signatures: export function searchHighlight(text: string, query: string): string
export function searchHighlight(query: string): (text: string) => string

assets.name: uniqueSlug
assets.summary: Turns a title into a URL slug that doesn't collide with the slugs already taken.
assets.useWhen: a new post, page or record needs a readable URL and some slugs are in use. The plain slug comes back when it is free, otherwise the first free `-2`, `-3`, … suffix.
signatures: export function uniqueSlug(title: string, taken: readonly string[]): string
export function uniqueSlug(taken: readonly string[]): (title: string) => string

assets.name: validateAddress
assets.summary: Checks a postal address form, with postal code and region rules that follow the country.
assets.useWhen: a checkout, shipping or billing form collects an address and should catch a missing city or a malformed ZIP before a carrier or payment provider rejects it. Every value is trimmed, and the country and postal code are uppercased; that tidied address is what comes back. Postal codes are checked for AU, CA, DE, EG, FR, GB, IN, JP, NL and US; other countries only get a length limit. A state or province is required in AU, CA and US.
signatures: export function validateAddress(address: ValidateAddressInput): Validation<ValidateAddressInput, FieldError<string>>

assets.name: validateAllOrNone
assets.summary: Checks a group of fields that only make sense together: all filled in, or all left empty.
assets.useWhen: an optional section of a form has parts that need each other, such as a card's number, expiry and CVC, a date and a time, or a billing address that may be left out. When some are filled and some aren't, each empty one gets a message naming the first filled field. `null`, `undefined`, a blank string and an empty array count as empty.
signatures: export function validateAllOrNone<T extends object>( record: T, keys: readonly (keyof T & string)[], ): Validation<T, FieldError<string>>
export function validateAllOrNone<T extends object>( keys: readonly (keyof T & string)[], ): (record: T) => Validation<T, FieldError<string>>

assets.name: validateAtLeastOne
assets.summary: Checks that at least one of several alternative fields is filled in, and flags them all if none is.
assets.useWhen: a form accepts one of a few ways to do the same thing, such as an email or a phone number to reach someone, or a file or a link for an attachment. When none is filled, each listed field gets the same message, so every one of them lights up. `null`, `undefined`, a blank string and an empty array count as empty.
signatures: export function validateAtLeastOne<T extends object>( record: T, keys: readonly (keyof T & string)[], ): Validation<T, FieldError<string>>
export function validateAtLeastOne<T extends object>( keys: readonly (keyof T & string)[], ): (record: T) => Validation<T, FieldError<string>>

assets.name: validateBirthDate
assets.summary: Checks a date of birth against a minimum age, refusing future dates and unlikely old ones.
assets.useWhen: sign-up, checkout or KYC must enforce an age limit such as 13, 18 or 21, and the person should read why they can't continue. Ages are whole years in UTC, so a birthday counts from the start of that day. A date that failed to parse arrives as `NaN` and is reported as missing. Pass `now`, so tests and servers in other time zones agree. The date comes back unchanged.
signatures: export function validateBirthDate(birthDate: number, rules: ValidateBirthDateRules): Validation<number, string>
export function validateBirthDate(rules: ValidateBirthDateRules): (birthDate: number) => Validation<number, string>

assets.name: validateBookingRange
assets.summary: Checks a stay's check-in and check-out days: not in the past, and a number of nights within limits.
assets.useWhen: a hotel, rental, parking or equipment booking form takes two dates and must refuse a past check-in, a zero-night stay or one longer than allowed, with each message under its field. Days are UTC calendar days, so times of day are ignored and today is a valid check-in. Nights are only counted once both dates are valid and check-in isn't in the past.
signatures: export function validateBookingRange( booking: ValidateBookingRangeInput, rules: ValidateBookingRangeRules, ): Validation<ValidateBookingRangeInput, FieldError<string>>
export function validateBookingRange( rules: ValidateBookingRangeRules, ): (booking: ValidateBookingRangeInput) => Validation<ValidateBookingRangeInput, FieldError<string>>

assets.name: validateCardNumber
assets.summary: Checks a payment card number's shape and Luhn checksum, and returns its digits without spaces.
assets.useWhen: a checkout form takes a card number and should catch a mistyped digit before the payment provider's round trip. Spaces and dashes are dropped first. The checksum only runs once the number has 12 to 19 digits and nothing else, so a typo gives one clear message. It doesn't say whether the card exists or what network it is; only the provider knows.
signatures: export function validateCardNumber(input: string): Validation<string, string>

assets.name: validateChoice
assets.summary: Matches typed or query-string input to one of the allowed choices, ignoring case and spaces.
assets.useWhen: a value arrives as free text, from a query string, a CSV column or a hand-edited config, and must become one of a fixed set, such as a size, plan or sort order. `' LARGE '` comes back as the choice's own spelling, `'Large'`, typed as the union of choices. The message lists the choices, so the person sees what to type.
signatures: export function validateChoice<C extends string>(input: string, choices: readonly C[]): Validation<C, string>
export function validateChoice<C extends string>(choices: readonly C[]): (input: string) => Validation<C, string>

assets.name: validateCouponCode
assets.summary: Tidies a promo, gift or invite code a person typed and checks its shape before it is looked up.
assets.useWhen: a checkout or sign-up form has a coupon, voucher, referral or invite code box, and `summer 25 ` should match the stored `SUMMER25`. Spaces are dropped and letters uppercased, and that tidied code is what comes back. A code is 4 to 20 letters, digits or dashes, not starting or ending with a dash. It checks the shape only; look the code up afterwards.
signatures: export function validateCouponCode(input: string): Validation<string, string>

assets.name: validateDateRange
assets.summary: Checks a start and end timestamp pair: both are real dates and the end is not before the start.
assets.useWhen: a report filter, booking or export form takes "from" and "to" dates and the server must refuse a range that runs backwards. Timestamps are milliseconds, so a date that failed to parse arrives as `NaN` and is reported as missing. An equal start and end is a valid zero-length range. The end is only compared once both dates are valid.
signatures: export function validateDateRange(range: ValidateDateRangeInput): Validation<ValidateDateRangeInput, FieldError<string>>

assets.name: validateEach
assets.summary: Runs a validator on every item of a list and reports each failing item by its index.
assets.useWhen: a list arrives from a form, CSV or request, such as invitees, line items or rows to import, and the person must see which entries are wrong, not just that some are. Every item is checked; each failing one gives one `{ index, errors }` with all its messages. On success the validator's outputs come back, so a validator that trims or parses changes the items.
signatures: export function validateEach<T, U, E>( items: readonly T[], validator: Validator<T, U, E>, ): Validation<U[], ValidateEachError<E>>
export function validateEach<T, U, E>( validator: Validator<T, U, E>, ): (items: readonly T[]) => Validation<U[], ValidateEachError<E>>

assets.name: validateEmailField
assets.summary: Checks an email form field and returns the trimmed address, with every problem as a message.
assets.useWhen: a sign-up, invite or contact form takes an email address and the field needs messages a person can act on. A blank field reports only that it is required, not also that its format is wrong. It doesn't lowercase the address, because the part before `@` can be case-sensitive: lowercase it yourself before checking whether the address is taken.
signatures: export function validateEmailField(input: string): Validation<string, string>

assets.name: validateEnvVars
assets.summary: Checks that every named environment variable is set, and returns just those, typed by name.
assets.useWhen: a server, worker or script starts up and must stop with one list of everything missing, instead of crashing later on the first `undefined`. Pass `process.env` and the names. A blank or whitespace-only value counts as missing. Values come back as they are, as strings; parse numbers and ports from the result.
signatures: export function validateEnvVars<K extends string>( env: ValidateEnvVarsSource, names: readonly K[], ): Validation<Record<K, string>, string>
export function validateEnvVars<K extends string>( names: readonly K[], ): (env: ValidateEnvVarsSource) => Validation<Record<K, string>, string>

assets.name: validateFileUpload
assets.summary: Checks an uploaded file's size and type against a policy, with messages that name the file.
assets.useWhen: a form or API accepts an avatar, attachment or import file, and an empty file, a 40 MB photo or an `.exe` should be refused before it is stored or processed. It reads `name`, `size` and `type`, so a browser `File` works as it is. It trusts the declared MIME type: check the file's bytes too when the upload is untrusted. Sizes in messages read like "11.8 MB". The file comes back unchanged.
signatures: export function validateFileUpload( file: ValidateFileUploadFile, policy: ValidateFileUploadPolicy, ): Validation<ValidateFileUploadFile, string>
export function validateFileUpload( policy: ValidateFileUploadPolicy, ): (file: ValidateFileUploadFile) => Validation<ValidateFileUploadFile, string>

assets.name: validateFileUploads
assets.summary: Checks a multi-file upload: each file's size and type, how many there are, and their total size.
assets.useWhen: an attachment picker, gallery or bulk import takes several files, and the person should see every refused file and every broken limit in one message list. Each file gets the same checks as `validateFileUpload`, named by file; the count and total size are checked on the whole list. The files come back unchanged and in order.
signatures: export function validateFileUploads( files: readonly ValidateFileUploadsFile[], policy: ValidateFileUploadsPolicy, ): Validation<readonly ValidateFileUploadsFile[], string>
export function validateFileUploads( policy: ValidateFileUploadsPolicy, ): (files: readonly ValidateFileUploadsFile[]) => Validation<readonly ValidateFileUploadsFile[], string>

assets.name: validateHexColor
assets.summary: Checks a hex color a person typed and returns it in one stored form: `#` and six lowercase digits.
assets.useWhen: a theme, brand or label editor takes a color, and `FFF`, `#fff` and `#FFFFFF` should all be stored the same way. The `#` is optional and the input is trimmed. Shorthand colors are expanded to six digits; eight-digit colors with alpha are kept and lowercased.
signatures: export function validateHexColor(input: string): Validation<string, string>

assets.name: validateJsonBody
assets.summary: Parses a JSON request body and checks it field by field, returning a typed object or every error.
assets.useWhen: a handler reads the raw body text, as in a Cloudflare Worker, a Lambda or a webhook whose signature is checked on the raw text, and needs a 400 answer listing every problem. Text that isn't JSON, or JSON that isn't an object, gives one error with `field: ''`. Otherwise each validator gets its raw value, `undefined` when absent, and returns the typed one. Only the declared fields come back; extra keys are dropped.
signatures: export function validateJsonBody<T>(text: string, fields: ValidateJsonBodyFields<T>): Validation<T, FieldError<string>>
export function validateJsonBody<T>(fields: ValidateJsonBodyFields<T>): (text: string) => Validation<T, FieldError<string>>

assets.name: validateMoneyAmount
assets.summary: Checks a money amount: a real number, inside the limits, with no more decimals than the currency has.
assets.useWhen: a payment, refund, invoice or transfer form takes an amount, and `19.999` dollars or `0` must be refused before it reaches a payment provider. The decimals follow the currency, so `1.5` is refused for JPY and `1.005` is fine for KWD. Limits in messages are formatted as money, like "$10,000.00". Float noise such as `0.1 + 0.2` doesn't count as an extra decimal, so computed totals pass. The amount comes back unchanged, not rounded. The currency is your configuration, not user input: an unknown code throws, as `Intl` does.
signatures: export function validateMoneyAmount(amount: number, rules: ValidateMoneyAmountRules): Validation<number, string>
export function validateMoneyAmount(rules: ValidateMoneyAmountRules): (amount: number) => Validation<number, string>

assets.name: validatePaginationParams
assets.summary: Reads `page` and `pageSize` from a query string, with defaults, and reports every bad one.
assets.useWhen: an HTTP handler for a list endpoint receives `?page=2&pageSize=50` and must answer 400 with clear messages for `page=0` or `pageSize=9999` instead of running a bad query. A missing or blank value takes its default: page 1 and `defaultPageSize`. Values are parsed as numbers, so `2abc` and `1.5` are refused. Pages are 1-based.
signatures: export function validatePaginationParams( query: ValidatePaginationParamsQuery, limits: ValidatePaginationParamsLimits, ): Validation<ValidatePaginationParamsResult, FieldError<string>>
export function validatePaginationParams( limits: ValidatePaginationParamsLimits, ): (query: ValidatePaginationParamsQuery) => Validation<ValidatePaginationParamsResult, FieldError<string>>

assets.name: validatePassword
assets.summary: Checks a new password against strength rules and lists every rule it breaks, in rule order.
assets.useWhen: a sign-up or change-password form should show all the missing pieces at once, such as "Add a number" and "Add a symbol", instead of one per submit. Only the rules you turn on run, besides the length limits. Letters count in any script, so `É` is uppercase. The password comes back unchanged: it is never trimmed.
signatures: export function validatePassword(password: string, rules: ValidatePasswordRules): Validation<string, string>
export function validatePassword(rules: ValidatePasswordRules): (password: string) => Validation<string, string>

assets.name: validatePasswordConfirmation
assets.summary: Checks a password and its repeat field together, with each problem under its own field.
assets.useWhen: a sign-up, reset or change-password form has "Password" and "Confirm password" inputs. You pass the rule for the password itself, such as `minLength(8)`, and this adds the repeat: a blank repeat asks for it, a different one says they don't match. Errors come back as `{ field, errors }`, ready to show under each input.
signatures: export function validatePasswordConfirmation( form: ValidatePasswordConfirmationForm, passwordRule: Validator<string, string, string>, ): Validation<ValidatePasswordConfirmationForm, FieldError<string>>

export function validatePasswordConfirmation( passwordRule: Validator<string, string, string>, ): (form: ValidatePasswordConfirmationForm) => Validation<ValidatePasswordConfirmationForm, FieldError<string>>

assets.name: validatePayload
assets.summary: Turns an unknown value, such as a parsed request body, into a typed object, field by field.
assets.useWhen: a handler gets `req.body`, a queue message or a webhook payload as `unknown`, and each field needs its own check and type before use. Each validator gets the raw value, `undefined` when the key is absent, and returns the typed value, so it can trim or convert. Only the declared fields come back; extra keys are dropped, so a stray `isAdmin` can't slip into an update. A value that isn't a plain object gives one error with `field: ''`.
signatures: export function validatePayload<T>(payload: unknown, fields: ValidatePayloadFields<T>): Validation<T, FieldError<string>>
export function validatePayload<T>(fields: ValidatePayloadFields<T>): (payload: unknown) => Validation<T, FieldError<string>>

assets.name: validatePhoneE164
assets.summary: Checks an international phone number and returns it in E.164 form, like `+14155550123`.
assets.useWhen: storing a phone number for SMS, calls or two-factor codes, where providers such as Twilio want E.164. Spaces, dots, dashes and brackets are dropped first, so `+1 (415) 555-0123` is fine. It checks the shape only, 7 to 15 digits after a `+` with a country code that doesn't start with 0; it doesn't know each country's numbering plan.
signatures: export function validatePhoneE164(input: string): Validation<string, string>

assets.name: validateQuantity
assets.summary: Checks an order quantity: a whole number, within the limits, and a multiple of the pack size.
assets.useWhen: a cart, order or booking form takes a quantity, and limits such as "at most 10 per customer" or "sold in packs of 6" must be explained to the buyer. A quantity that is not a whole number reports only that. Otherwise every broken limit is listed.
signatures: export function validateQuantity(quantity: number, rules: ValidateQuantityRules): Validation<number, string>
export function validateQuantity(rules: ValidateQuantityRules): (quantity: number) => Validation<number, string>

assets.name: validateRequiredFields
assets.summary: Checks that the named fields of a record are filled in, with one "X is required" per gap.
assets.useWhen: a form or request body has several required fields whose own format is checked elsewhere, and you want every missing one reported together. `null`, `undefined`, a blank string and an empty array count as missing; `0` and `false` count as filled. Messages turn the key into words: `firstName` becomes "First name is required".
signatures: export function validateRequiredFields<T extends object>( record: T, keys: readonly (keyof T & string)[], ): Validation<T, FieldError<string>>
export function validateRequiredFields<T extends object>( keys: readonly (keyof T & string)[], ): (record: T) => Validation<T, FieldError<string>>

assets.name: validateRows
assets.summary: Checks every row of a list against one schema and reports errors at paths like `lines[2].qty`.
assets.useWhen: a form or request carries a list of objects, such as order lines, invitees or spreadsheet rows, and each bad cell must be shown next to its input. Every row and every field is checked. Each failing field gives one `{ field, errors }`, its `field` being the list name, the row index and the field name, the shape form libraries use for nested inputs.
